page: Amazon Web Services m8idb.large is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The configuration supplies 2 virtual CPUs derived from a single dedicated Intel physical core running at a 3.9 GHz clock frequency on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 8.0 GB of main memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance operates without discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

A key component of the hardware configuration is the inclusion of integrated instance storage. The m8idb.large includes 118 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, providing low-latency, high-throughput direct disk access for applications requiring fast local read and write operations. Network capabilities are established at a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Resource allocation balances compute power and memory capacity with fast ephemeral storage, making it cost-efficient for applications that benefit from local caching rather than relying solely on remote network storage volumes. Due to its dual-thread compute boundary and 8.0 GB memory capacity, this instance is suited for moderate web serving, CI/CD runners, caching layers, small relational databases, and light analytics workloads that require fast local disk scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idb.large is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The hardware deployment includes 2 vCPUs running on a single dedicated Intel physical core clocked at 3.9 GHz across the x86_64 architecture. Memory is sized at 8.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Unlike standard general-purpose offerings, the instance incorporates 118 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD instance storage, enabling high IOPS and low-latency disk access for temporary data. Network connectivity delivers a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The server operates without a GPU and is designed for balance across core compute, system memory, and localized disk operations. Its architectural balance makes it suitable for application tiers, microservices, continuous integration agents, and local database environments requiring high-speed temporary storage.
